legal.draftNotice: Initial draft for demonstration. Needs legal counsel review before launch; items in [ ] are to be completed.

s1.p: SALEEM is an advisory tool that helps creators review content before publishing against an illustrative rulebook. It never grants an official approval or license.

s2.p: You are responsible for the decision to publish, the accuracy of the details you enter, and your right to upload the content.

s3.p: Don't upload unlawful content or other people's content without permission, or try to access other users' data.

s4.p: The service is subject to monthly plan limits. [Pricing and payment details to be added].

s5.p: The service is provided as is. We don't guarantee content is free of violations after a check. [Final wording by legal counsel].

s6.p: These terms are governed by the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. [Jurisdiction to be specified].

s1.p: [Legal entity name, address and CR number]. Data enquiries: [data protection officer email].

s2.p: Account data (name, email, optional Mawthooq license number), the content you upload, and check results.

s3.p: We process data to provide the checking service, based on your consent and the contract, under the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL).

s4.p: Video, frames and audio are deleted automatically 24 hours after a check. Findings and the file hash are kept while your account exists.

s5.h: Processors and transfers outside the Kingdom
s5.p: We use a database hosting provider and an AI model provider to analyze content; processing may occur outside the Kingdom. [List of processors, processing locations and safeguards].

s6.p: We don't sell your data or share it with any regulator or advertiser, and we don't use your content to train models.

s7.p: You can access, correct, port and delete your data. Download your data or delete your account directly from Settings.

s8.p: [Request channel, response time, and right to lodge a complaint with the competent authority].

s1.p: SALEEM results are advisory alerts, not an official approval from any government body. The final decision is yours.

s2.p: The rulebook was drafted for illustration from public sources and is pending legal review.

s3.p: The system may miss violations or flag acceptable content. Review the findings yourself and consult a specialist when needed.

s1.p: Timed speech transcript, one frame per second (up to 60), on-screen text, the caption and post details.

s2.p: Fixed automatic rules catch disclosures, discount codes and explicit claims; a vision language model understands context. We merge both and remove duplicates.

s3.p: Weak-evidence findings are shown as warnings, not violations; subjective rules (privacy, wealth display, attire) are always warnings.

s4.p: We measure per-rule hits, misses, false alarms and timestamp error on a Saudi-dialect test set. Current results come from a small set and don't cover every case.

s5.p: Transcription can confuse similar words or struggle with noise, and the model can misjudge age or context. We never identify people.

s6.p: Every report records the model, prompt version and rulebook version, and each compliance log is sealed with a publicly verifiable fingerprint.
